land.text: the Taurus castles of Ermenek, Mut, Ereğli, Gülnar and Silifke, and Larende, held from the Seljuks of Rum (infobox 'Preceded by: Sultanate of Rum')

predecessors.note: Larende and Ermenek were given c. 1260 by Kilij Arslan IV; Mut was fought over with Cilician Armenia in 1260.

land.text: Karaman Eyalet, 'founded from former territories of Karamanids': the plateau (Konya, Larende) annexed 1468, the Taurus rump at Silifke in 1487

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Ottoman Empire'. Cliopatria's row ends in 1467; the page ends the state in 1487.

capitals.name: Larende (Karaman)
capitals.note: The infobox lists 'Larende; Ermenek; Konya (1307–1468); Mut; Ereğli; Silifke (1474–1487)', years only for Konya and Silifke; Larende (with Ermenek) was given to Karaman Bey c. 1260. Ermenek is also listed as a capital.

capitals.name: Konya
capitals.note: Infobox 'Konya (1307–1468)'. Konya changed hands several times (1277, 1308, early 14th century to Chupan); the Ottoman annexation of Konya is 1468 (infobox). Konya was taken by Bayezid I in 1390 (Bayezid I page) and is drawn back with the Karamanids from 1391 (confidence 1), so the span is split.

capitals.name: Larende (Karaman)
capitals.note: 1390 only, a reading (confidence 1): the Bayezid I page has Konya, 'their capital', taken in 1390 and names no other seat; Larende is the infobox's first-listed capital.

capitals.name: Konya
capitals.note: Second span: Konya after the 1391 peace (page silent on terms; infobox 'Konya (1307–1468)' without a break), to the Ottoman annexation of the city (1468 on the infobox; Cliopatria's shape ends 1467).

capitals.name: Mut
capitals.note: The infobox lists Mut and Ereğli among the capitals without years; placed between the end of Konya (1468) and the start of Silifke (1474) by the order of the list only (confidence 1).

rulers.name: Nure Sofi
rulers.note: Table of rulers on the Karamanids page; the infobox founding is c. 1255, the table starts in 1250 (Anatolian beyliks table: 1250). Karaman Bey, discussed as founder in the body, is not in the table.

rulers.name: Karim al-Din Karaman
rulers.note: Table 1256-1263; the body says Karaman Bey died in 1262.

rulers.name: Mehmed I
rulers.note: Table to 1277; the body has him executed in 1278 after Konya.

rulers.name: Alaattin Ali
rulers.note: Table 1361-1398. Bayezid I defeated and killed 'the emir of Karaman' at Akçay in 1397 (Bayezid I page, which does not name him).

rulers.name: Erhan
rulers.note: Reigned while the state was an Ottoman vassal (infobox 1398-1402).

rulers.name: Mehmed II
rulers.note: Table 1402-1423; Alaattin Ali II (1420-1421) is listed inside this span. Timur 'gave control of the Karamanid lands to Mehmet Bey'.

rulers.name: Alaattin Ali II
rulers.note: Overlaps Mehmed II in the table.

rulers.name: Ibrahim II
rulers.note: Mehmed II page: 'İbrahim escaped to a small city in western territories where he died in 1464.'

rulers.name: Turgutoğlu Mahmut II
rulers.note: A Mustafa Beg (rebellion, 1500-1501) follows in the table, after the 1487 end; not listed.

correction.text: the 1305 shape (the Taurus country round Larende, Ermenek, Mut and Silifke) projected back to 1255

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1305 but the infobox says 'Established c. 1255' and Karaman Bey held 'castles in Ermenek, Mut, Ereğli, Gülnar, and Silifke' (the page reports 1225 for those conquests and calls it 'excessively early'). The page gives no extent before 1305, so the 1305 shape stands in; approximate. No area on the page.

Years only: unchanged shape, 27,701 km2, valid 1305-1307. The page has no infobox area. Konya passes to the Karamanids in 1308 (infobox 'Conquest of Konya: 1308') and Cliopatria's 1314 shape takes the plateau.

correction.text: the 1314 shape from the Karamanid conquest of Konya in 1308: Konya, the Karaman country and the plateau to Aksaray and Niğde

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the infobox dates the 'Conquest of Konya' to 1308 and gives Konya as capital from 1307, but Cliopatria draws the plateau (81,771 km2) only from 1314, the year after its Sultanate of Rum row ends (1313). The sultanate-of-rum dossier ends Rum in 1308 and hands 'Konya and the plateau' to Karaman, so the 1314 shape is used from 1308. Extent beyond Konya is Cliopatria's, not the page's; no area on the page.

81,771 km2 for 1314-1325 (Konya, Karaman, Niğde, Aksaray plateau). The page gives no area and no boundary; it says only that 'Karamanids captured Konya on two more occasions at the beginning of the 14th century' and were 'driven out the first time by emir Chupan, the Ilkhanid governor of Anatolia' (no dates). The shape is kept as Cliopatria draws it; the Ilkhanid overlordship is recorded in the ilkhanate dossier.

91,156 km2: 30 cells (about 9,400 km2, bbox 31.3-32.5 E, 37.2-38.2 N: Lake Beyşehir and the country west of it, by my reading) are added on the west in the year Cliopatria's Eshrefids row ends (1325). The Eshrefids dossier has the Ilkhanid viceroy Timurtash take Beyşehir on 9 October 1326. The Karamanids page says nothing on this; verified only that it lies next to the core.

99,408 km2: a strip north-west of Konya (29 cells, bbox 31.1-32.2 E, 38.6-39.5 N) is added in 1333. The page supports a general expansion: 'An expansion of Karamanoğlu power occurred after the fall of the Ilkhanids in the 1330s' (infobox: de facto independent sultanate from 1332). No page names the places.
99,626 km2, one cell more than 1333 (grid noise); no page explains a change in 1344.

91,375 km2: the 29-cell strip north-west of Konya added in 1333 drops out in 1352 (to no Cliopatria state). Page silent; unverified: page budget. The ruler table has three changes of bey in 1349-1352.
100,291 km2: the strip returns in 1363 (31 cells) under Alaattin Ali (table 1361-1398). Page silent; unverified: page budget. This is the largest shape of the row; the page offers no area.

correction.text: unchanged shape; it holds 1385-1389 only: in 1390 Akşehir, Niğde and Konya pass to Bayezid I (beylik-of-karaman_1390), from 1391 the shape returns (beylik-of-karaman_1391) until Bayezid I annexes the emir's territory in 1397

keyframe_review.note: Years only: unchanged shape, valid 1385-1389. Cliopatria runs it to 1401, but 'In a single campaign over the summer and fall of 1390' Bayezid I took 'Akşehir and Niğde, as well as their capital Konya from the Karaman', accepted peace proposals in 1391, and 'In 1397, Bayezid defeated the emir of Karaman in Akçay, killing him and annexing his territory' (Bayezid I page); the Karamanids infobox lists 'Vassal state of Ottoman Sultanate (1398-1402)'. The two pages disagree on annexation versus vassalage; the ledger follows the Bayezid page (loss 1397, gain 1402) like the sibling dossiers of Saruhan and Menteshe. The Karamanids infobox lists 'Battle of Frenkyazısı: 1386' and the Murad I infobox '1387', without detail on either page.

union.text: Akşehir (38°21′27″N 31°24′59″E, Akşehir page; no gazetteer place)

minus.text: Akşehir, Niğde and 'their capital Konya from the Karaman' (Bayezid I page)

correction.text: the 1385 shape less Akşehir, Niğde and Konya, taken by Bayezid I in the campaign of 1390

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, one year: 'In a single campaign over the summer and fall of 1390' Bayezid I took Akşehir, Niğde and 'their capital Konya from the Karaman'. The page names no other loss; the discs are 30-40 km radii round the three cities (a reading).

correction.text: the 1385 shape again, with Konya, Akşehir and Niğde, after the peace of 1391

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, confidence 1: 'Bayezid accepted peace proposals from Karaman (1391)'; the page gives no terms and does not say the three cities were returned. Drawn as the full 1385 shape to 1396 because the 1397 annexation takes 'his territory' and the Karamanids infobox keeps Konya as capital without a break.

99,804 km2 for 1402-1406: 'Timur gave control of the Karamanid lands to Mehmet Bey, the oldest son of Aleaddin Ali Bey' (undated on the page; the infobox status returns to de facto independent in 1402 and the Battle of Ankara is 20 July 1402, Bayezid I page). The extent of the restored beylik is not given; the Cliopatria shape is the pre-1397 shape.

Years only: 100,143 km2, 339 km2 more than 1402 (grid noise); no page explains a change in 1407. 'In 1411, Kütahya fell to Mehmed II of Karaman' and 'Mehmed Chelebi reinstated Yakub's rule in Germiyan in 1414' (Germiyanids page), so for 1411-1413 the shape holds Kütahya as well; Kütahya lies outside this shape (see the 1411 keyframe).

correction.text: unchanged shape for 1407-1410 and 1414-1428; in 1411-1413 Kütahya is added (beylik-of-karaman_1411)
the 1407 shape plus Kütahya, held by Mehmed II of Karaman 1411-1413

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1411, Kütahya fell to Mehmed II of Karaman' and 'Mehmed Chelebi reinstated Yakub's rule in Germiyan in 1414' (Germiyanids page). The page does not say who held Kütahya in 1412-1413; the 30 km disc is the Germiyanids dossier's own zone.

100,239 km2 for 1429-1462. 'The Karamanids were defeated in 1428' (Murad II page) with no land change named; Cliopatria adds one cell from Germiyan in 1429. The Karamanids page names no loss of land to Murad II. Verified only that the plateau stays Karamanid.

100,270 km2, 1463-1467. 'captured both Karaman (Larende) and Konya in 1466' (Mehmed II page) while the Karamanids infobox has 'Annexation of Konya: 1468'. The shape is kept to Cliopatria's last year 1467; the ledger has the fighting from 1466 and the annexation in 1468.

correction.text: the Taurus rump round Mut and Silifke, the part of the 1467 shape in Mersin province

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape after 1467 but the infobox gives 'Rump state (1474-1487)' with Silifke as capital 1474-1487, and 'The Karamanid state was eventually terminated by the Ottomans in 1487'. The extent of the rump is not on the page: the part of the 1467 shape inside Mersin province (Mut, Silifke, the Taurus coast) is used; the years 1468-1473 are a bridge (confidence 1). The ottoman-empire dossier gains the whole 1467 shape in 1468 and should leave this rump out until 1487.

region.text: the Taurus castles of Ermenek, Mut, Ereğli, Gülnar and Silifke, with Larende

ledger.note: c. 1255: Karaman Bey founds the Karamanid principality in the Taurus. Infobox 'Established: c. 1255'; 'Karaman Bey expanded his territories by capturing castles in Ermenek, Mut, Ereğli, Gülnar, and Silifke' (the page's 1225 for these conquests 'seems excessively early'). The Anatolian beyliks table has the rule from 1250; the ruler table of this page starts in 1250.

region.text: the town of Larende (now Karaman) and Ermenek

ledger.note: c. 1260: Kilij Arslan IV gives the Karamanids Larende and Ermenek. 'he gave the town of Larende (now Karaman, in honour of the dynasty) and Ermenek (c. 1260)'.

region.text: Mut, site of the 1260 battle (no gazetteer place)

ledger.note: 1260: Mut passes to the Karamanids. Infobox 'Battle of Mut: 1260'; the page does not say who held Mut. The armenian-kingdom-of-cilicia dossier records the loss of Mut and Ermenek to the Karamanids in 1260, which is the reason for the counterpart; the year is the page's, the land and counterpart are the reading.

region.text: Konya, the Seljuq capital

ledger.note: 12 May 1277: Mehmed Bey takes Konya from the Seljuks of Rum. 'Mehmed Bey captured Konya on 12 May' (a note on the page gives 1276 for the same capture); 'In the Battle of Göksu in 1277 in particular, the central power of the Seljuq was dealt a severe blow.'

region.text: Konya

ledger.note: 1278: the Karamanid hold on Konya ends. Mehmed was 'defeated by Seljuq and Mongol forces and executed with some of his brothers in 1278'. The sultanate-of-rum dossier closes its contest in 1277; the page gives 1278 for the defeat.

region.text: Karaman's land, under Ilkhanid suzerainty

ledger.note: 1305 (a reading): the Karamanids are drawn as an Ilkhanid dependency, mirroring the ilkhanate dossier's vassal_start of 1305 (confidence 1, Cliopatria's year). The Karamanids page never uses the word vassal: it has Konya lost to 'emir Chupan, the Ilkhanid governor of Anatolia' and to 'Chupan's son and successor Timurtash' (both undated), and in 1277-78 Mehmed was 'defeated by Seljuq and Mongol forces'. It dates the end of the dependency only as 'An expansion of Karamanoğlu power occurred after the fall of the Ilkhanids in the 1330s'.
1307: the Karamanid seat moves to Konya (infobox 'Konya (1307–1468)'); the conquest of Konya is dated 1308 on the same infobox.

region.text: Konya, the Karaman country and the plateau to Aksaray and Niğde, the shape Cliopatria draws from 1314

ledger.note: 1308: the Karamanids conquer Konya and the Seljuk plateau. Infobox 'Conquest of Konya: 1308'. The extent beyond Konya is Cliopatria's 1314 shape (Niğde, Aksaray); the sultanate-of-rum dossier hands 'Konya and the plateau' to Karaman in 1308. The page adds that the Karamanids 'captured Konya on two more occasions at the beginning of the 14th century' and were 'driven out the first time by emir Chupan'.

region.text: the western strip added to the shape in 1326 (about 30 cells, Lake Beyşehir and the country west of it)

ledger.note: 1326 (page silent): Cliopatria adds a strip west of the core (Lake Beyşehir and the country west of it) in the year its Eshrefids row ends. The Eshrefids dossier has the Ilkhanid viceroy Timurtash take Beyşehir in October 1326, so the Ilkhanate is the counterpart; how the strip reached the Karamanids is on no page opened (confidence 1). Rechecked 2026-10-25: the Eshrefids page says only that the dynasty 'ended when Mubariz al-Din Mehmed was executed by Timurtash', names no Karamanid successor and says nothing of Beyşehir after 1326; the Karamanids page has Alaeddin Ali capturing Beyşehir 'which had been an Ottoman city' without a year. Still a gap (confidence 1).

region.text: the strip north-west of Konya added in 1333

ledger.note: 1330s: the Karamanids expand as the Ilkhanids fall. 'An expansion of Karamanoğlu power occurred after the fall of the Ilkhanids in the 1330s.' The year 1333 and the land (a strip north-west of Konya) are Cliopatria's; no Cliopatria state held the cells before, hence 'nobody'.

region.text: Karaman's land

ledger.note: 30 November 1335: Abu Said dies and the Ilkhanid governorship of Anatolia ends with him. Abu Sa'id page: 'died on his way in Karabakh on the night of 30 November 1335' (the infobox says 1 December); Karamanids page: 'An expansion of Karamanoğlu power occurred after the fall of the Ilkhanids in the 1330s'. Mirrors the ilkhanate dossier's vassal_end of 1335 (confidence 1); neither page says the Karamanids were released on that day.

region.text: the strip north-west of Konya lost in 1352 and regained in 1363

ledger.note: 1352 (page silent): the north-western strip drops out of Cliopatria's shape for ten years, to no other Cliopatria state. The page names no event; the table shows three changes of bey between 1349 and 1352 (confidence 1). Rechecked: the Karamanids reign table has Şemseddin 1350-1352 and Hacı Sufi Musa's second reign from 1352, a change of ruler in the year the strip leaves Cliopatria's shape; the Murad I page is silent. Still a gap.

region.text: the strip north-west of Konya regained in 1363

ledger.note: 1363 (page silent): the strip north-west of Konya returns to Cliopatria's shape under Alaattin Ali (table 1361-1398); no page opened names the land or the neighbour (confidence 1). Rechecked: the Karamanids page gives Alaattin Ali 1361-1398 and the Murad I page (marriage to Nefise Hatun in 1378 'in an unsuccessful attempt to stop the war') no land; neither mentions Konya's north-west. Still a gap.

union.text: Akşehir (38°21′27″N 31°24′59″E, Akşehir page; no gazetteer place)

region.text: Akşehir, Niğde and 'their capital Konya from the Karaman' (Bayezid I page)

ledger.note: 1390 (summer and fall): Bayezid I takes Akşehir, Niğde and the capital Konya from the Karamanids. Bayezid I page: 'In a single campaign over the summer and fall of 1390', after the conquest of Aydin, Saruhan and Menteshe, he 'overwhelmed the remaining beyliks (Hamid, Teke, and Germiyan)' and took Akşehir and Niğde, 'as well as their capital Konya from the Karaman'. No month; only the three cities are named, so the rest of the Karaman country is taken to stay (the Taurus and the western strip), a reading (confidence 2). The Akşehir page agrees only that the town 'late in the 14th century passed into Ottoman hands' and that Akşehir and Beyşehir were the Ottoman-Karamanid border, 'changing hands several times'.
1390 (a reading): with Konya lost the Karamanid seat falls back on Larende (Karaman), the infobox's first-listed capital; the Bayezid I page names no new seat.

union.text: Akşehir (38°21′27″N 31°24′59″E, Akşehir page; no gazetteer place)

region.text: Akşehir, Niğde and 'their capital Konya from the Karaman' (Bayezid I page)

ledger.note: 1391 (a bridge over a silence): peace with Bayezid I. 'At this point, Bayezid accepted peace proposals from Karaman (1391)'. The page gives no terms and does not say Konya, Akşehir or Niğde were returned. They are drawn back with the Karamanids because the Karamanids infobox lists Konya as capital 'Konya (1307–1468)' without a break and because the 1397 campaign annexes 'his territory', which Cliopatria draws as the whole 1385 shape (confidence 1; if the three cities stayed Ottoman until 1397, delete this gain and the keyframe beylik-of-karaman_1391).
1391 (a reading, with the gain above): the seat returns to Konya (infobox 'Konya (1307–1468)').

region.text: 'his territory', the emir of Karaman's land: the whole 1385 shape

ledger.note: 1397: Bayezid I defeats the Karamanids at Akçay and annexes their territory. 'In 1397, Bayezid defeated the emir of Karaman in Akçay, killing him and annexing his territory.' The page names no place; the whole Karaman shape is the reading. The Karamanids infobox calls 1398-1402 a vassal period ('Vassal state of Ottoman Sultanate (1398–1402)'), a milder reading of the same years.

region.text: the Karamanid lands, restored to Mehmed Bey (Mehmed II of Karaman)

ledger.note: 1402: Timur restores the Karamanid lands after Ankara. 'Timur gave control of the Karamanid lands to Mehmet Bey, the oldest son of Aleaddin Ali Bey' (undated on the page; the infobox restores the de facto independent status in 1402; the Battle of Ankara is 20 July 1402 on the Bayezid I page).

region.text: Kütahya

ledger.note: September 1410: war between Karaman and Germiyan. 'This escalated to a war between the two in September 1410' (Germiyanids page); the page gives no earlier campaign and Kütahya is the place that changes hands. Mirrors germiyanids /ledger/10.

region.text: Kütahya

ledger.note: 1411: Kütahya falls to Mehmed II of Karaman and the fighting ends in a Karamanid hold; no treaty is on the page. Mirrors germiyanids /ledger/11.

region.text: Kütahya

ledger.note: 1411: Mehmed II of Karaman takes Kütahya. 'In 1411, Kütahya fell to Mehmed II of Karaman (r. 1398–1399, 1402–1420), interrupting Yakub's reign a second time.' No month. Kütahya lies outside every Cliopatria shape of Karaman; the keyframe beylik-of-karaman_1411 adds a 30 km disc. Mirrors germiyanids /ledger/12.

region.text: Kütahya

ledger.note: 1414: Kütahya returns to Germiyan. 'Mehmed Chelebi reinstated Yakub's rule in Germiyan in 1414' (Germiyanids page; its infobox has Kütahya as Germiyanid capital '1402–1411, 1414–1429'). The Mehmed I page lists 'Campaign of Karamanids (1414)' and the Karamanids infobox an 'Ottoman-Karamanid War' of 1413-1415, without detail. The page does not say who held Kütahya in 1412-1413; Karaman is the counterpart. Mirrors germiyanids /ledger/13.

region.text: Karaman (Larende) and Konya and the plateau

ledger.note: 1466: Mehmed II takes Larende and Konya. 'captured both Karaman (Larende) and Konya in 1466' (Mehmed II page). The Karamanids infobox dates the 'Annexation of Konya' to 1468, so the zone is drawn contested from 1466 to 1468.

region.text: the plateau round Konya and Larende

ledger.note: 1468: the Ottomans annex Konya and the plateau. Infobox 'Annexation of Konya: 1468'; the Mehmed II page has the capture in 1466, and Cliopatria's row ends in 1467.

region.text: Konya, Larende and the plateau, the 1467 shape less the Taurus rump

ledger.note: 1468: Konya and the plateau pass to the Ottomans; the Karamanids keep the Taurus coast. Infobox 'Annexation of Konya: 1468' and, later, 'Rump state (1474-1487)'. The ottoman-empire dossier's own 1468 gain takes the whole 1467 shape and should exclude the rump until 1487.
1474: the rump state's seat is Silifke (infobox 'Silifke (1474–1487)'; 'Rump state (1474-1487)').

region.text: the Taurus rump round Mut and Silifke

ledger.note: 1487: the Ottomans take the last Karamanid land. 'The Karamanid state was eventually terminated by the Ottomans in 1487'; 'Ottomans founded Karaman Eyalet from former territories of Karamanids.'

region.text: the whole remaining state, the Taurus rump

ledger.note: 1487: the Karamanid state ends. 'The Karamanid state was eventually terminated by the Ottomans in 1487, as the power of their Mameluke allies was declining.' (Infobox 'Disestablished: 1487'.)

wars.name: Karamanid capture of Konya (1277)
wars.outcome: The Karamanids take Konya on 12 May 1277 and install a pretender; Mehmed Bey is 'defeated by Seljuq and Mongol forces and executed with some of his brothers in 1278'.
wars.note: The page's table gives Mehmed's reign to 1277, the body his execution in 1278; a note gives 1276 for the capture.

wars.name: Bayezid I's campaigns against the Karamanids

union.text: Akşehir (38°21′27″N 31°24′59″E, Akşehir page; no gazetteer place)

zones.text: Akşehir, Niğde and 'their capital Konya from the Karaman' (Bayezid I page)

wars.outcome: In the summer and fall of 1390 Bayezid took Akşehir, Niğde and 'their capital Konya from the Karaman'; he 'accepted peace proposals from Karaman (1391)' (no terms on the page) before turning on Kastamonu; in 1397 he defeated and killed the emir at Akçay and annexed his territory; the Karamanids infobox lists a vassal period 1398-1402.
wars.note: The infobox also lists 'Battle of Frenkyazısı: 1386' without detail on the page. Timur restored the Karamanid lands after the Battle of Ankara (20 July 1402).

wars.name: Battle of Ankara and the Timurid restoration of Karaman
wars.outcome: Bayezid I's army is defeated on 20 July 1402 (Bayezid I page: 'In 1400, Timur succeeded in rousing the local Turkic beyliks'); Timur gives the Karamanid lands to Mehmed Bey.
wars.note: No border is contested; the restoration is the ledger's 1402 gain.

wars.name: Murad II's campaigns against the Karamanids
wars.outcome: 'The Karamanids were defeated in 1428' and the infobox lists 'Campaign in Karamanids (1444)'; the page names no land that changed hands.
wars.note: Karamanid İbrahim Bey 'marched on Ankara and Kütahya, destroying both cities' in 1443-44 in the years of the Crusade of Varna (Karamanids page); no gain.

wars.name: Mehmed II's conquest of Karaman
wars.outcome: Mehmed II captures Karaman (Larende) and Konya in 1466 (Mehmed II page); the Karamanids infobox dates the annexation of Konya to 1468, a rump state at Silifke 1474-1487, and the end of the state to the Ottomans in 1487.
wars.note: The Mehmed II page does not give the 1468 annexation; Pir Ahmed 'died in 1474'. Mamluk support for the Karamanids is mentioned without dates.

wars.name: Karaman, Germiyan and the Ottomans over Kütahya (1410-1415)
wars.outcome: War between Karaman and Germiyan from September 1410; Kütahya falls to Mehmed II of Karaman in 1411 and Mehmed Çelebi reinstates Yakub in Germiyan in 1414 (Germiyanids page); the Karamanids infobox gives an 'Ottoman-Karamanid War' of 1413-1415.
wars.note: Mehmed II of Karaman 'further laid siege to Bursa for 31 days in 1413' (Germiyanids page); the Mehmed I page lists 'Campaign of Karamanids (1414)' without detail. Kütahya is the only land change named.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a treaty line or a survey for the Karamanids; the Taurus, plateau and western frontiers are approximate throughout.

notes:
Row identity: Cliopatria's 'Beylik of Karaman' (Wikipedia 'Karamanids', Q1469100, Seshat tr_karaman_bey) is one state, 1255-1487 on the page. Cliopatria's row covers 1305-1467, so two new keyframes bracket it: 1255-1304 (the 1305 shape projected back, approximate) and 1468-1487 (the Taurus rump at Mut and Silifke, the part of the 1467 shape in Mersin province). The page gives no extent for either.
Page budget (up to 5): Karamanids, Anatolian beyliks, Bayezid I, Mehmed II, Murad II. No page gives an area, so no infobox ratio is possible. Shapes 1314-1363, 1407 and 1429 are verified only as 'plausible core'; the strip north-west of Konya (29-31 cells) that appears in 1333, vanishes in 1352 and returns in 1363 rests on Cliopatria alone (confidence 1 events).
Disagreements: (1) 1397 Ottoman annexation 'annexing his territory' (Bayezid I page) against the infobox 'Vassal state of Ottoman Sultanate (1398-1402)'; the ledger follows the annexation (loss 1397, gain 1402, as the sibling dossiers of Saruhan and Menteshe do) and the ottoman-empire dossier (me-10) should carry a gain in 1397 and the loss in 1402 or a vassal_start for beylik-of-karaman 1398-1402. (2) Mehmed II page: Larende and Konya captured in 1466; infobox: annexation of Konya 1468; drawn contested 1466-1468. (3) Rulers table against body (Mehmed I 1277 or 1278; Karim al-Din 1262 or 1263; Alaattin Ali II overlaps Mehmed II). (4) The ottoman-empire dossier gains the whole 1467 shape in 1468 and nothing in 1487: it should leave the Taurus rump (this dossier's beylik-of-karaman_1468) out until 1487.
Cross-dossier: the ilkhanate dossier carries vassal_start 1305 and vassal_end 1335 for beylik-of-karaman; the fix pass mirrors both here at confidence 1 (counterpart ilkhanate). The germiyanids dossier records Kütahya to Karaman in 1411 and back in 1414; the fix pass mirrors the events (contest 1410-1411, gain 1411, loss 1414) and adds the keyframe beylik-of-karaman_1411. The armenian-kingdom-of-cilicia dossier has the 1260 loss of Mut and Ermenek to Karaman (mirrored). The mamluk-sultanate and beylik-of-dulkadir dossiers may hold the Tarsus and Konya episodes the page leaves undated ('Ramazanoğlu Ali Bey captured Tarsus while Mehmet Bey was in prison'; 'The Egyptian Mamluks damaged Konya after defeating the Karamanids'); not dated, so not in the ledger.
Not settled: the 1293 'Siege of Alanya' (infobox, no outcome); the 1261 march on Konya with 20,000 men (no result); the 1225 conquests (page: 'excessively early'); the Mamluk attack on Konya; the Bursa raid of Mehmet Bey (undated); the extent of the restored beylik after 1402. Status change 1332 (beylik to de facto independent sultanate, infobox) is not an event for the map. Gazetteer: Ermenek, Mut, Silifke, Eflani-type places are absent from places.jsonl; coordinates are used.
Fix pass (author, reviewer me-09-e): (1) 1390 loss of Akşehir, Niğde and Konya to Bayezid I (Bayezid I page, confidence 2) and a 1391 gain back at confidence 1 because the page gives no peace terms; keyframes 1385 (years 1385-1389), 1390 and 1391, the Konya capital span (split, with Larende in 1390) and the war follow. If the three cities stayed Ottoman from 1390 to 1397 the 1391 gain, its capital_move and keyframe 1391 are the events to delete. (2) Kütahya events mirrored from the Germiyanids page. (3) Ilkhanid vassal_start 1305 / vassal_end 1335 mirrored at confidence 1: the Karamanids page names Chupan and Timurtash as the Ilkhanid governors who drove the Karamanids from Konya but never calls them vassals; disagreement with none, the ia-02 events stay a reading. (4) Thin items reopened, still thin: the Eshrefids, Karamanids and Murad I pages say nothing on who took the Beyşehir strip in 1326 or on the 1352/1363 strip; the Ilkhanate still has no loss for the 1326 strip (route to ia-02). Gazetteer: Akşehir is not in places.jsonl (coordinates from the Akşehir page used, 30 km).
